claims.text: An RHEA interlayer between W and CuCrZr will mitigate their thermal-expansion mismatch.
An RHEA interlayer will suppress interdiffusion between W and CuCrZr.
Mitigating thermal-expansion mismatch and suppressing interdiffusion will enhance W/CuCrZr interfacial stability under fusion-reactor conditions.
W and CuCrZr substrates are used in current reactor designs.
Directly bonded W and CuCrZr have known interfacial-stress problems.
Directly bonded W and CuCrZr have known diffusion problems.
RHEAs are promising materials for elevated-temperature and advanced-nuclear applications.
The proposed RHEA interlayer can be engineered through composition changes and optimized using diffusion-bonding experiments.
High temperature, high heat flux, thermal cycling, and inert-atmosphere or high-vacuum exposure represent the intended simulated fusion-reactor conditions.
A tailored RHEA grain structure will create a graded interface between W and CuCrZr.
The RHEA will have an intermediate thermal-expansion coefficient that accommodates the property mismatch between W and CuCrZr.
The RHEA will act as a diffusion barrier because of low atomic diffusivity.
The intermediate thermal-expansion properties of the RHEA will reduce mechanical stresses.
The RHEA interlayer will inhibit formation of brittle intermetallic phases.
Reduced interdiffusion and thermal stress will improve mechanical integrity and long-term stability of the bonded W/CuCrZr structure.
Direct W/CuCrZr bonding commonly produces pronounced interdiffusion and high interfacial stresses because of mismatched thermal expansion and diffusion behavior.
Extreme irradiation or unforeseen chemical interactions may limit the RHEA interlayer's effectiveness.
The long-term irradiation behavior of the proposed interlayer remains uncharacterized.
SEM, EDS, residual-stress measurements, and mechanical tests can compare an RHEA-containing joint against a directly bonded W/CuCrZr control.
The hypothesis is falsified if the RHEA-containing joints fail to reduce interdiffusion and residual stress and fail to improve mechanical performance relative to the control.
